1-10.text: Read the following passage and answer the given questions. Finding the right person has never been easy. But in recent years, dating apps powered by Artificial Intelligence have tried to make this process simpler and smarter for millions of people around the world. Today, these apps do much more than just show a list of nearby profiles — they study user choices, learn preferences, and suggest matches that are most likely to be a good fit. What was once a matter of luck has gradually become a matter of data. The way AI works inside these apps is not difficult to understand. Every time a user swipes left or right, starts a conversation, or spends extra time looking at a particular profile, the app quietly records that behaviour. Over time, the AI uses all of this information to grow more accurate in the kind of matches it recommends. The more a person uses the app, the better it understands what they are genuinely looking for — going far beyond simple filters like age and location to pick up on patterns that even the user might not have noticed about themselves. From a business point of view, AI has helped dating app companies capture a much larger share of the overall digital matchmaking market. Platforms that use intelligent personalisation consistently perform better than those that rely on basic search tools. When users feel that an app truly understands their preferences, they are far more likely to continue using it and paying for premium features. This growing base of loyal, paying users has made AI investment a top priority for every major dating platform operating today. AI has also changed how these apps approach the problem of user safety. Automated systems now detect fake profiles, flag inappropriate messages, and verify photographs — making the overall experience considerably safer than it was in the early days of online dating. Not everyone, however, is comfortable with the idea of an algorithm deciding who they should meet. Many users feel that love, by its very nature, should involve a degree of _________________ that no machine can fully replicate or plan for.

Conclusions:

II. V = Y

If only conclusion II is true.
If either conclusion I or II is true.
If neither conclusion I nor II is true.
If both conclusions I and II are true.

Eight persons – A, B, C, D, E, F, G, and H – live in a four-storey building (but not necessarily in the same order), where the lowermost floor is numbered as 1 and the floor immediately above it is numbered as 2, and so on.

items.x: Sum of the 9th and 10th numbers = 1015 − 640 − 250 = 125 and their difference is 5, so the 9th = 65.

items.q: The present age of A is 50% more than B and the ratio of A’s age five years ago to B’s age ten years hence is 1 : 2. Find the sum of present age A & B?
items.x: A = 1.5B and 2(A − 5) = B + 10 give B = 10, A = 15; sum 25.

The speed of a boat in still water is 20 km/hr and the ratio of downstream to upstream speed of the boat is 5 : 3 respectively. Find the time taken by the boat to cover 240 km downstream (in hours).
items.x: (20 + s)/(20 − s) = 5/3 gives s = 5, so downstream speed = 25 and time = 240/25 = 9.6 h.

items.q: 2/3rd of first number is equal to the cube of the second number. If the second number is equal to 12% of 100, then what is sum of the first & second number?
items.x: Second number = 12; first = 1.5 × 12³ = 2592; sum = 2604.

66-69.text: Read the following information carefully and answer the questions given below. The information about fiction and non-fiction books in three different books stores. The ratio of the non-fiction books in A to fiction books in B is 5:3, respectively. The fiction books in C are 20 more than those of B, and the total books (fiction + non-fiction) in C are 200, which is 20% less than those of A. Non-fiction books in B are 60, and the average fiction books in all the stores is 100.
66-69.sol: Total in A = 200 ÷ 0.8 = 250. Fiction A + B + C = 300 and fiction C = fiction B + 20. Non-fiction A = (5/3) × fiction B, and fiction A + non-fiction A = 250 → fiction B = 90, fiction C = 110, fiction A = 100, non-fiction A = 150, non-fiction C = 90.
